summary: Wave 2: zero-shot DRIFT (co-occurrence diffusion) across 5 BEIR corpora vs lexical and SPLADE, synthesized

per_corpus.vs_splade: below — drift recall 0.9056 vs SPLADE 0.909 (−0.0034); recovers ~91% of the lexical→SPLADE gap but does not beat the GPU model. Lexically strong (0.876 lexical) so little semantic gap to mine; nDCG drops 0.6712→0.5108.

ABOVE — drift recall 0.2841 vs SPLADE 0.282 (+0.0021). Zero-shot, no-GPU DRIFT BEATS GPU SPLADE on this mismatch (medical) corpus; biggest gain (+0.0462) and heaviest expansion (alpha=0.4). nDCG dips only 0.3071→0.2925.

far below — drift recall 0.5078 vs SPLADE 0.61 (−0.102). Optimizer chose alpha=0 (no expansion): co-occurrence diffusion was net-harmful and got dialed out. SPLADE clearly wins; use lexical+SPLADE fusion, not drift.
no SPLADE ref. alpha=0 chosen, recall stays 0.0949 (recall@100 is low because trec-covid has very deep pools/many relevants); nDCG strong at 0.5617 unchanged. Drift adds nothing here.
no SPLADE ref. alpha=0 chosen, recall 0.5579 unchanged, nDCG 0.3161 unchanged. Argument-retrieval co-occurrence too noisy to help; drift dialed out.

synthesis.general_finding: DRIFT (corpus co-occurrence diffusion, no model/no GPU) is a SELECTIVE, not reliable, zero-shot semantic-recall lever. It helped on only 2 of 5 corpora — scifact (+0.0297) and nfcorpus (+0.0462) — and on the other 3 (fiqa, trec-covid, touche) the per-corpus alpha optimizer drove expansion weight to 0, meaning the diffusion was net-harmful and was switched off. Where it helps, it works by attacking the semantic gap (gold docs sharing no literal query word), and the effect is larger on lexical-mismatch corpora (nfcorpus 0.4 alpha) than on lexically-aligned ones (scifact 0.8 alpha, small headroom over its already-high 0.876 lexical recall). It is a RECALL lever that trades nDCG for recall — scifact nDCG 0.6712→0.5108, nfcorpus 0.3071→0.2925 — so expansion noise must be cleaned up by a reranker after retrieval. Headline result: on nfcorpus, zero-shot no-GPU DRIFT (0.2841) actually BEATS GPU SPLADE recall@100 (0.282), and on scifact it closes to within 0.0034 of SPLADE (0.9056 vs 0.909) — but on fiqa SPLADE is far ahead (0.61 vs 0.5078) and drift contributes nothing.
where_drift_beats_splade: nfcorpus: drift recall@100 0.2841 > SPLADE 0.282 (+0.0021), zero-shot no-GPU beating the GPU model on a medical mismatch corpus
synthesis.recommendation: Deploy DRIFT selectively, gated by a per-corpus alpha sweep (let the optimizer pick alpha; if it picks 0, ship pure lexical). Per corpus: nfcorpus → DRIFT as a recall booster (it beats SPLADE zero-shot, +0.0462 over lexical) then rerank to recover the small nDCG dip; scifact → DRIFT to lift recall toward SPLADE (+0.0297, reaches 0.9056) but always rerank since nDCG drops sharply (0.6712→0.5108), and if SPLADE/GPU is available prefer it or fuse since it still edges drift; fiqa → DO NOT use drift (alpha=0, no gain), use SPLADE or lexical+SPLADE RRF fusion (SPLADE leads by +0.102 recall); trec-covid → lexical only (drift adds nothing, nDCG already strong 0.5617); webis-touche2020 → lexical only (drift dialed out, too noisy). General rule: DRIFT first as a cheap no-GPU recall lever on mismatch corpora, then rerank; fall back to lexical wherever the alpha sweep returns 0.
synthesis.notes: Drift does NOT help where (a) the corpus is lexically strong with little semantic gap to mine — scifact already has 0.876 lexical recall, so expansion gains are small and bought at a steep nDCG cost; and (b) co-occurrence is too noisy/diffuse to expand reliably — on fiqa, trec-covid, and webis-touche2020 the per-corpus optimizer set alpha=0, i.e. any expansion hurt recall, so drift collapsed to pure lexical. The alpha pattern is informative: mismatch corpus nfcorpus rewards aggressive expansion (alpha=0.4), aligned scifact only tolerates light expansion (alpha=0.8 = mostly lexical). Build cost is trivial/no-GPU (0.9s–35s, scaling with doc count: nfcorpus 3633 docs/0.9s up to touche 382545 docs/35.3s). Caveat: best_drift_ndcg is reported at the recall-optimal alpha, so the nDCG figures reflect the recall-tuned operating point, not a precision-tuned one — confirming drift is a recall-stage lever that needs a rerank stage after. SPLADE references used: scifact 0.909, nfcorpus 0.282, fiqa 0.61 (no SPLADE ref for trec-covid/touche, so 'beats SPLADE' is undetermined there).
